newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling gunning for break of 2.90 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling gunning for break of 2.90 marks.

text.p: Sterling will pause to gather its strength before making a fresh attempt to break above 2.90 marks for the first time in almost five years, analysts said.

"This rally does not seem like it is going to finish," said Joachim Goldberg, global head of technical analysis at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Frankfurt. "Sterling/mark looks set to test 2.9070 and, further out, 2.9150 seems to be on the cards."
Sterling/mark, which set a 59-month high of 2.8945 overnight, was at 2.8909/19 at 0750 GMT against 2.8897/02 late on Friday. Cable was at $1.6624/34 against $1.6614/24 Friday.

Sterling's surge above 2.8820 marks on Friday spurred analysts at Chase Investment Bank to target further gains up to the upper boundary of an ascending channel which has been developing over the past six months.
Trendline resistance cuts in at 2.9040 marks on the daily charts and "a daily close above here would open further upside potential towards 2.9445 and 2.9480", they said.
Former resistance of 2.8820 marks has turned into support for the pound, and sterling must now hold above it if optimism about its prospects is to remain intact, technical analysts said.
"Sterling has strengthened its support in the 2.8790/2.8820 zone but if it goes below there, it will trigger a technical correction down to 2.5560," said Goldberg at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
While cable has failed to match sterling/mark's progress, it has found solid support around $1.6600, testing and quickly rebounding from this level on each of the last four trading days.
As long as cable holds above this area, analysts still favour an eventual break of the five-month high of $1.6725 which has capped its progress since June 23.
